historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR 0.6% is the honest recent trend (FY2022-25 revenue flat at RMB110-112bn as gas-price pass-through deflated the top line while volumes grew); the 5yr 9.3% is inflated by the FY2021-22 gas-price spike. Equity CAGR 7-9% is retained earnings on a ~50% payout, not operating growth, and cannot be the revenue driver. Base path uses 2.5-3.0%, roughly Chinese gas-volume growth less price deflation.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.4% diverges by far more than 30% from EPS 5yr CAGR -0.9% and revenue 3yr CAGR 0.6%: book value compounds through retained earnings while per-share earnings have been flat-to-down since the FY2021-22 peak (core profit RMB7,966m FY2022 -> RMB6,741m FY2025). Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) series: FY2020 3,846; FY2022 3,153; FY2025 3,259 (RMB m). Owner and reported CAGRs are within ~0.6pp of each other because SBC is negligible; the gap is interest income shrinking from RMB204m to RMB123m. Both series are flat-to-negative over 3 and 5 years: capex (RMB5.6bn FY2020 -> RMB7.1bn FY2025) absorbed all of the growth in operating cash flow (RMB9.7bn -> RMB10.4bn).

scenario_narratives.base: Mature concession utility: low-single-digit volume growth, gradual residential pass-through completion lifting EBITDA margin from 10.6% to 11.0%, connection fees in structural decline, capex normalising from 2.0x to 1.4x D&A. Owner-FCF margin rises from ~2.9% to ~4%. Parent's ~35% stake is an overhang, not a catalyst, until the Takeovers Code restriction expires ~June 2027.
scenario_narratives.bull: Pass-through completes and tariff reform holds; policy-driven volume growth of 4%; electricity-centric integrated energy and smart home become margin contributors; EBITDA margin 11.8%, capex 1.35x D&A. A renewed, cash-heavier parent offer after June 2027 is the unmodelled upside.
scenario_narratives.bear: Pass-through stalls into an LNG price spike; property downturn erases the connection-fee pool; integrated energy stays a capex sink; working capital unwinds; EBITDA margin 9.5%, growth 1-1.5%, capex 1.5x D&A. Parent sits at 35% without bidding.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ENN Energy is valued as a mature, concession-protected cash-flow stream in RMB at a CNY-built 7.5% WACC, with the thin owner-FCF margin (capex 2x D&A) explicitly normalising over ten years rather than being carried forward. The three scenarios are organised around this company's real axes: the pace of residential gas-price pass-through versus wholesale cost volatility, the structural decline of connection fees under China's property downturn, whether the integrated-energy capex sink earns a return, and what the controlling shareholder does with its ~35% stake after the privatisation scheme lapsed on 12 June 2026. Risk is charged once, in the flows and weights; the same WACC applies to every scenario. Associates/JVs, NCI, financial assets and the June-30 dividend payable are bridged at 30 June 2026 values so that every income stream stripped from EBITDA has its matching asset.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory pass-through: 25% of residential volume still unrepriced; municipal tariff hearings are slow and politically sensitive, and a wholesale LNG/oil spike reopens the margin lag
Connection-fee decline: construction/installation revenue -17.9% FY2025 and -26.7% H1 2026 as new residential hookups fall with China's property market
Capex normalisation is the main value driver: if capex stays at 2x D&A (integrated energy, PV, storage) owner FCF stays near 3% of revenue and the base case is overstated

Parent overhang: ENN Natural Gas holds ~35% after the scheme lapsed and is barred from a new general offer until ~June 2027; a low-ball renewed offer or indefinite stake-building caps the minority's exit
Currency: flows are RMB, quote is HKD; a weaker RMB lowers the HKD value one-for-one, and 61.5% of USD1.04bn debt is unhedged

Bridge judgments: associates/JVs (+RMB9.7bn) and NCI (-RMB9.2bn) are valued at 10x earnings; moving both to book would add ~RMB4.3bn (~HK$4.5/share); the stripped dividend income's FVTPL assets (RMB4.0bn) are at carrying fair value

data_sources.qualitative: 2688.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-22): business model, pass-through progress, scheme lapse and parent accumulation, segment trends

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,131,839,264 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim report, note 3). This INCLUDES the ~20m shares (1.77%) held in trust for the Share Award Scheme, which the diluted-EPS count of 1,111.9m excludes; they will be awarded to employees, so the issued count is the conservative divisor and makes the scheme's dilution explicit in the denominator rather than in an SBC charge. Options are anti-dilutive per the interim. Held FLAT: no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.net_debt_note: H1 2026 interim MD&A net-debt table: total debts RMB18,944m (bank and other loans 9,461 + 2,435, senior notes 3,740 + 3,308) less bank balances and cash RMB8,554m (excluding RMB200m restricted deposits). Lease liabilities (110 current + 463 non-current) are NOT in total_debt because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Net gearing 19.1% of total equity per the company.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation (AR p.96) carries no share-based payment add-back; share-based payment liabilities RMB3m at FY2025. The Share Award Scheme is funded by on-market purchases (RMB665m FY2024, RMB229m FY2023, nil FY2025 and H1 2026) and those shares are already inside the 1,131.84m issued count used as the divisor, so SBC is charged once, through the share count. Forward SBC held at 0% of revenue as an explicit row (SBC-zero market convention).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025: nil. FY2024: RMB665m repurchased under the Share Award Scheme (held in trust, not cancelled). No general buyback programme; the flat count is a modelling convention the company funds only episodically via the award-scheme trustee.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.175 (Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22, same fetch as the price). Statements and all flows are RMB; the H-share quote is HKD, so every RMB per-share value is multiplied by 1.175. No dual listing of ENN Energy exists for a parity check (the parent 600803.SH is a different entity); direction check: the HKD price / 1.175 x 1,131.84m shares gives a market cap of ~RMB46.7bn and a trailing P/E of 7.9x on FY2025 attributable profit of RMB5,904m, matching the ~7.8x screen figure in the Analysis JSON. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-source it on each price refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T03:58:47Z (Yahoo chart API, intraday HK session; 52-week range 40.38-73.80)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: China 10y CGB ~1.8%. ERP 6.5%. Beta 0.9 for an H-share city-gas distributor gives a cost of equity of ~7.7%; rounded up to 8.5% to recognise, once and only in the discount rate, the persistent HK-listed-China-minority discount the market demonstrably prices (the stock yields 6.2% on a 7.9x P/E). Pre-tax cost of debt 3.3% (FY2025 interest RMB710m on ~RMB19.3bn average borrowings = 3.7%, falling with PRC policy rates), 2.5% after 25% tax. Capital weights 80/20 equity/debt at market (market cap RMB46.7bn, net debt RMB10.4bn). WACC = 0.8 x 8.5 + 0.2 x 2.5 = 7.3%, used as 7.5%. The SAME 7.5% applies to all three scenarios: regulatory, commodity and parent-overhang risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in a per-scenario WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease payment (FY2025 principal RMB187m + lease interest RMB32m = RMB219m, 0.20% of revenue) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (RMB573m at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A RMB3,486m = 3.12% of revenue; ~0.17pp of that is ROU, so the path starts at 3.0%) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of EBITDA/capex), so NCI is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 10x FY2025 NCI profit share (RMB919m -> RMB9,190m; book RMB6,312m at 30 June 2026, NCI dividends RMB798m FY2025). FY0 cross-check: FY2025 EBIT 8,512 x (1-25%) = NOPAT 6,384; + share of associates/JVs 967 - net finance cost 470 = 6,881 vs reported profit incl. NCI of 6,823 + other gains/losses 543 = 7,366 pre-non-core items; ties within non-operating noise.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Operating EBITDA = gross profit + other income - interest income - dividend income - distribution & selling - administrative + D&A. Excludes share of results of associates/JVs (RMB967m FY2025), other gains and losses (RMB-543m: FX, derivative fair value, ECL and PP&E impairments, disposal losses), finance costs and interest/dividend income. FY2025: 13,292 + 669 - 123 - 148 - 1,386 - 3,792 = EBIT 8,512; + D&A 3,486 = EBITDA 11,998 (10.72% of revenue). FY2024 on the same definition: 11,994 (10.92%). The cash-flow statement's pre-working-capital operating cash of RMB11,989m reconciles to it. Every stripped income stream has its asset in equity_bridge (associates/JVs, FVTPL/FVTOCI); interest income's asset is the cash netted in net_debt.
inputs.fy0_component_check: FY2025 component rebuild: EBITDA 11,998 - lease 219 - cash tax 2,136 (25.1% of EBIT ex lease interest) - capex 7,051 (6,718 PP&E and other non-current assets + 333 intangibles) + working capital 580 = 3,172 unlevered owner FCF, vs last_fcf 3,259 (reported FCF 3,382 - interest income 123). Owner-FCF margin 2.9%: capex has run at 1.9-2.0x D&A for three years (integrated-energy build-out), which is why FCF is thin against RMB6.7bn of core profit; H1 2026 capex fell to 4.4% of revenue as management 'flexibly managed the pace of expenditures'.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, probability-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: an operating company (city-gas distribution, 264 concessions, plus integrated energy and smart home), not a bank/REIT/LIC, so the standard engine applies with the non-US adaptations (CNY WACC, HKD quote, leases treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching assets in bridge). The routing table's 'live takeover' row does NOT apply: the ENN Natural Gas privatisation scheme LAPSED on 12 June 2026 and the Takeovers Code bars a renewed general offer until ~June 2027; the parent's on-market accumulation (~35% by Sept 2026) is carried as an overhang/optionality in the narrative and weights, not as a deal-completes scenario. 10-year horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still normalising (capex/D&A gliding from 2.0x to 1.4x). SBC is zero so house and street coincide; band_position is null by construction. Price is an intraday HK print and should be replaced at the regular close. Equity bridge items (associates/JVs, NCI, financial assets, dividend payable) are all dated 30 June 2026 and applied identically across scenarios.

bear.narrative: Bear: tariff reform stalls at the municipal level while an international LNG/oil price spike reopens the pass-through lag, so retail gas margin compresses rather than recovers; China's property downturn keeps new connections falling 20%+ a year and the construction/installation profit pool largely disappears; integrated energy keeps absorbing capex without earning its cost of capital; contract liabilities (advance gas fees and construction deposits, RMB13.1bn) unwind as a working-capital outflow; the unhedged 61.5% of USD1.04bn debt adds FX cost. EBITDA margin drifts to 9.5%, growth 1-1.5%, capex stays at 1.5x D&A. The parent, at ~35% with no obligation to bid, lets the minority sit; the stock stays a yield instrument with a shrinking coupon.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 (Y1) 2.5%: H1 2026 printed +2.4% with retail gas volume growth offset by construction/installation -26.7% and integrated energy -8.6%. Y2-4 3.0% as pass-through repricing (74.8% of residential volume done) adds price to volume; fades to 2.5% terminal, below Chinese nominal GDP, because connection fees are in structural decline.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 operating EBITDA margin 10.72% (10.92% FY2024). Y1 10.6% holds the two-period core-profit decline (-3.0% FY2025, -1.5% H1 2026); recovers 0.1pp/yr to 11.0% as residential pass-through narrows the retail-gas dollar-margin gap, offset by the lower-margin wholesale mix growing fastest. Does not return to the FY2021-22 level.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 capex 6.3% of revenue (2.0x D&A); FY2023-24 5.9-6.1%; H1 2026 4.4%. Glides to 4.8% (1.4x D&A) by Y10 as new-connection and integrated-energy build-out moderates and the electricity pivot runs asset-lighter via trading/VPP. D&A ex-ROU rises from 3.0% to 3.4% as the recent build depreciates.
base.tax_rationale: PRC statutory 25%; FY2025 cash tax RMB2,136m = 25.1% of EBIT. No carryforwards or one-offs to ramp from; held flat.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% implies 20.5x terminal FCF; capped at 15x, the upper end of the 12-15x band the method prescribes for a slower, regulated business. The cap is expected to bind.
base.narrative: Base: ENN remains a mature, concession-protected gas distributor growing volumes low-single-digit; residential pass-through completes gradually and lifts retail gas margin enough to offset the structural decline in connection fees; integrated energy stabilises and smart home grows but neither moves group margin much; capex normalises toward 1.4x D&A, which is what turns a 2.9% owner-FCF margin into ~4% by year 10. The parent's ~35% stake is a standing overhang that is neither a floor nor a catalyst in this case.

bull.narrative: Bull: residential pass-through reaches ~90%+ of volume within three years and NDRC tariff reform keeps the retail dollar margin at or above the regulated benchmark; the bottle-to-pipeline policy and 15th Five-Year-Plan equipment-renewal programmes keep C/I and residential volume growth at 4%; the electricity-centric integrated-energy pivot (14.7GW, +40% electricity sales) turns from a capex sink into a margin contributor, and smart home scales across the 32.8m-household base; capex falls toward 1.35x D&A. EBITDA margin recovers to 11.8%, still below the FY2021-22 peak. Once the 12-month Takeovers Code restriction expires (~June 2027) the parent, already at ~35%, returns with a cash-heavier offer and the minority gets a premium exit, though that premium is not modelled here beyond the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: core profit has fallen two periods running, the thesis depends on a single regulator (NDRC/municipal tariff hearings) honouring pass-through, and the lapsed scheme leaves a controlling shareholder with no obligation to minorities. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs pass-through completion, construction stabilisation and the integrated-energy pivot all to work at once. Base 50%. The parent's post-June-2027 optionality is treated as symmetric (bid premium vs. indefinite overhang) and not weighted separately because the scheme is dead and no new offer can be made for 12 months.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
